summary: George Chemparathy studied Indology and philosophy under Erich Frauwallner (~1962–1967) and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as professor at Utrecht University from around 1973 to 1993.

George Christopher Molesworth Birdwood, an Indology and history/archaeology scholar, earned an M.D. at the University of Edinburgh (~1849–1854). He taught at Grant Medical College (~1858–1868), curated the Government Museum, Chennai, and served at the India Office (1878–1899).

George Cowgill was an archaeologist who studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Harvard University (~1956–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2013).

George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London (~1861–1862). He held an academic post at University College London from around 1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès worked in archaeology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at EPHE under Alfred Foucher, Louis Finot, and Sylvain Lévi. He directed the EFEO (1929–1947), curated the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929), and held several later teaching posts in France.

George D. Bond worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968–1972) and studying at the University of Sri Lanka. He served as Professor of Religion at Northwestern University from around 1974 to 2011.

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago (1902) and Harvard University (1903–1905). He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George Ernest Ward worked in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He completed his education in England, studying at The Queen's College, Oxford, and earning an M.A. at Wadham College, Oxford (~1856–1860).

George Eugene Dunkel, a linguist and Indologist, earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1976) and studied under Karl Hoffmann. He taught at Johns Hopkins (1975–1978) and Princeton (1978–1986) before taking a chair at the University of Zurich in 1986.

George Everest studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1804–1806). Active in Indology, he served as an assistant at the Great Trigonometrical Survey in 1817 and as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1830 to 1843.

George F. Dales studied at the University of Akron and the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. ~1953–1960). In archaeology and Indology, he held posts at the Royal Ontario Museum, University of Pennsylvania (1963–1972), and UC Berkeley (appointed 1972).
George Fletcher MacMunn was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich in 1888 and later served as Warden of Sackville College from 1939 to 1952.

George Foot Moore studied at Yale (1870–1872) and Union Theological Seminary (~1872–1877). A religious studies scholar, he taught at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and held professorships at Harvard University (1902; 1904–1928), with a guest professorship in Berlin (1909–1910).

George Frederick Nicholl, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned an M.A. from Balliol College, Oxford (ending 1878). He served as Lecturer in Oriental Languages at Oxford (1878–1909) and Professor of Sanskrit and Persian at King's College London (1879).
George Gordon Rogers was active in linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at Bedford College and attended the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst around 1912 to 1913.

George Henry Rouse worked in religious studies and Indology, studying at Regent's Park College (~1856–1861) and the University of London (~1858–1861). He served as a teacher at Haverfordwest Baptist College from 1867 to 1872.

George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who was educated at Phillips Academy (~1856–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He spent his academic career holding a post at Harvard University from around 1870 to 1913.
George Herbert Westcott, a scholar in religious studies and Indology, earned a B.A. at Peterhouse, Cambridge (1882–1885). In 1894, he held an appointment as a Fellow at the University of Allahabad.

George L. Hart, an Indologist and linguist, earned his Sanskrit PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1964–1971). He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1975) and served as professor at UC Berkeley (~1975–2014; Emeritus ~2014).

George Lakoff, a linguist and philosopher, studied at MIT and Indiana University Bloomington (Promotion ~1962–1966), also studying under Roman Jakobson. He taught linguistics at Harvard (1965–1969) and was a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley (1972–2016).
